title: A Wronskian Identity for Antisymmetrized Sine Sums: unconditional denominator positivity via circular convolution, sharp monotonicity distinctions, and counterexamples to naive sine-series principles
abstract: For real arrays (a_m) and (b_m) satisfying sum m(|a_m|+|b_m|) < infinity, we prove the exact Wronskian identity collapsing the antisymmetrized sine double sum to W(t) = 2[F_a'(t)F_b(t) - F_a(t)F_b'(t)] with explicit Fubini justification. Applying this to the modified-Bessel arrays (A_m, B_m) of the companion two-dimensional lattice gauge surface-positivity problem, we prove unconditionally for every beta > 0 that F_B(t) = -(f^{*4})'(t)/(2 I_1(beta)^4) > 0 on (0, pi) via fourfold normalized circular convolution of f(t) = exp(beta cos t), together with non-asymptotic super-exponential Bessel decay bounds. We establish the exact implication chain in the real-analytic Bessel family while showing via exact finite counterexamples that generic reverse implications fail: F_a/F_b = cos^3 t (W(pi/2)=0), a=(6,10,24), b=(6,5,2) (near-pi negative yet W(2pi/3)=51*sqrt(3)>0), and a=(3,4,3), b=(3,2,1) (non-monotone via two opposite signs W(pi/2)=-32<0 and W(2pi/3)=3*sqrt(3)>0). The finite Wronskian identity is machine-checked in Lean 4/Mathlib (release yang-mills-archive-v1.0); the global Bessel Wronskian negativity conjecture remains open.

editorial.statement: Working-paper version v3 supersedes v2. Declared minor revision: v3 resolves all minor polish notes from gpt-6.2-sol on v2: adds the explicit second sign evaluation W(pi/2) = -32 < 0 in Proposition 8 alongside W(2pi/3) = 3*sqrt(3) > 0 to prove nonmonotonicity with two opposite signs, explicitly starts the r_{k-1} consequence in Lemma 3 at k >= 1 with explicit O_beta decay rates, completes the Bessel implication diagram, labels Remark 10 digit counts as empirical heuristics, and pins the exact repository release and commit hash. It remains outside the AIRR accepted collection until this exact version passes review and receives a human decision.
